title: Yankees Activate Max Fried From Injured List After 10-Week Elbow Recovery
excerpt: The left-hander returns to start Game 2 of Wednesday’s doubleheader against the Pirates, joining Gerrit Cole in the rotation for the first time since signing his $218 million deal.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Max Fried returns after 10 weeks on the injured list, starting Game 2 against the Pirates.
  • Fried and Gerrit Cole pitch together for the first time as Yankees teammates.
  • Fried has a 4-3 record and 3.21 ERA in 2026, following a strong 2025 season.
  • His return may influence the Yankees' strategy ahead of the August 3 trade deadline.
  • Yankees starters have a 3.63 ERA, ranking fifth in the majors despite injuries.

Fried Activated Ahead of Schedule

The New York Yankees activated left-hander Max Fried from the 15-day injured list on Wednesday between games of their day-night doubleheader against the Pittsburgh Pirates at Yankee Stadium, according to Reuters. Fried will start the nightcap, marking his first major league appearance since May 13.

https://x.com/Yankees/status/2080038057877631160

Fried, 32, was placed on the injured list on May 14 with a bone bruise in his throwing elbow after his velocity dropped during a three-inning outing against the Baltimore Orioles. He had originally been slated for a second minor league rehab start on Wednesday, but the Yankees accelerated his timeline after Tuesday’s game was rained out.

“He’s capable of that. When he gets it rolling, he’s capable of big things.”

— Aaron Boone, Yankees manager, on the team’s offensive potential

To make room on the roster, the Yankees optioned right-hander Kervin Castro to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. Castro, 27, had allowed one run over 2 1/3 innings since being called up during Sunday’s doubleheader against the Los Angeles Dodgers.

A Historic Pairing Finally Arrives

Wednesday’s doubleheader marks the first time Fried and fellow ace Gerrit Cole have been in the Yankees rotation simultaneously. Cole, who was recovering from Tommy John surgery throughout Fried’s dominant 2025 season, made his 2026 debut on May 22 — eight days after Fried landed on the injured list.

The dual-ace pairing was a central part of the Yankees’ long-term planning when they signed Fried to an eight-year, $218 million contract ahead of the 2025 season. In his first year in the Bronx, Fried delivered a 19-5 record and 2.86 ERA across 32 starts, earning his third All-Star selection.

Cole (3-5, 3.93 ERA) started the afternoon opener against Pittsburgh’s Mitch Keller, while Fried drew right-hander Bubba Chandler (3-8, 4.77) in the nightcap. Fried carries a 4-1 record with a 3.94 ERA in eight career starts against the Pirates.

Strong Start Preceded May Struggles

Fried’s 2026 season splits into two distinct stretches. Through seven April starts, he posted a 4-1 record with a 2.09 ERA, a 1.01 WHIP, and a .199 opponents’ batting average across 47 1/3 innings. His 50-to-19 strikeout-to-walk ratio reflected the elite command that made him one of baseball’s most reliable starters.

May brought a sharp downturn. In three starts covering 14 1/3 innings, Fried allowed 11 earned runs and 17 hits while walking seven batters — just five fewer walks than he had accumulated in his first seven outings combined. His monthly ERA ballooned to 6.91 before the elbow injury ended his season’s first act.

Fried completed one rehab start with Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre last Friday, throwing 52 pitches over three innings. He allowed two runs on five hits, struck out three, and did not walk a batter. NBC Sports reported he would likely be limited to roughly 60 pitches in his return.

Rotation Relief With Trade Deadline Looming

Fried’s return arrives at a pivotal moment for the Yankees. Outside of Cy Young front-runner Cam Schlittler, New York’s rotation has been inconsistent, and left-hander Carlos Rodón remains on the injured list with left elbow inflammation. The NY Post reported that Rodón could return by early August, which would give the Yankees their dream rotation of Schlittler, Cole, Fried, Rodón, and either Will Warren or Ryan Weathers.

The Aug. 3 MLB trade deadline looms, and Fried’s health and performance in his first few starts back could determine how aggressively general manager Brian Cashman pursues pitching reinforcements. The 10-year veteran carries a career 96-44 record with a 3.04 ERA across 210 appearances.

Yankees starters have posted a 3.63 ERA entering this week, the fifth-best mark in the majors, despite the extended absences of both Fried and Cole for significant stretches. With both aces now available, the second-half rotation picture looks considerably brighter for a team with postseason aspirations.
